column1: # Every third-party package in the resolved closure of the platform's proposed transport set,
# with the licence read from the package's own published manifest at crates.io on 2026-08-21 -
# The gate reads this file. A package in Cargo.lock that is not
# attested here, or attested at a different version, fails the build.
# Two findings are recorded rather than left in the data:
#   R-efi offers "MIT OR Apache-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1-or-later". We elect MIT. The platform
#   admits no copyleft at runtime in any layer, so the LGPL option is refused deliberately
#   rather than passed over. r-efi is a UEFI platform crate and is not built on a Linux node.
#   The closure was reduced from 201 packages to 161 by selecting native-tls over the default
#   rustls path. That removed aws-lc-sys - a large C crypto library needing a compiler at build
# - and webpki-root-certs, whose CDLA-Permissive-2.0 is not on the allow-list and would have
#   needed explicit review. The prior research fleet already used native-tls; the reduction was
#   Keyed by name AND version, not by name. Three crates resolve at two versions each
#   (getrandom, syn, windows-sys). Keying by name alone dropped one version of each and left
#   three packages unattested - caught by reconciling the attested count against the lock,
#   which is why the two numbers are checked against each other rather than trusted.
#   Extended 2026-08-21 with the cryptographic closure the key derivation requires. argon2 is taken at
#   0.5.3, its stable line - the newest published version is a release candidate, which would
#   have failed the stable-release disqualifier quietly, because a version number rarely looks
#   Extended again 2026-08-22 with the TOML closure the configuration parser requires.
#   Extended 2026-08-23 with two packages the transport pulled that the earlier probe did
#   not: futures-macro and log. The gate refused the manifest until they were read at source,
#   which is what it is for.
#   Extended 2026-08-23 again, with the rustls/ring closure. The dependency record explains why
#   the TLS backend changed: native-tls needs OpenSSL headers this machine does not have.
# Twenty-one further rows added on 2026-08-30 for the second venue's signing set,
# each licence read the same way - from the package's own published manifest, fetched and
# opened, not from the index summary and not from memory.
# The count is by (name, version) and not by name. Three of the twenty-one - const-oid,
# hmac and sha2 - are names this file already carried at a different version, and counting
# names would have left them unattested with the gate reading (name, version).
# Thirty-one rows added on 2026-11-03 for the research archive: parquet 60.1.0 with default
# features off and zstd on, and its closure. Licences read from each package's published
# manifest in the local registry. zstd-sys builds the bundled zstd C library (BSD-3-Clause) and
# needs a C compiler at build time. r-efi 5.3.0 carries the same election as 6.0.0 above: MIT.
# The windows, android, haiku and wasi rows are target-specific and not built on a Linux node.
# One row added on 2026-11-03 for the data engine's stop handling: signal-hook-registry 1.4.8,
# which tokio's signal feature brings. Licence read from its published manifest in the registry.
# 2026-11-26: the venue websocket moved to sockudo-ws 3.1.1 (permessage-deflate). Its closure was
# added with each licence read from the package's own manifest in the registry, and tungstenite,
# tokio-tungstenite and the two packages only they brought were removed.
